title: Neck Pain After Desk Work in Winnipeg: When to Book Physio
excerpt: Neck pain affecting work or driving? See what to track before an assessment and how to book neck pain physiotherapy in St. Vital, Winnipeg.
intro: Your neck feels fine at breakfast, then stiff by midafternoon. By the time you finish work, turning to check traffic feels uncomfortable. That pattern is worth describing clearly; it does not, by itself, identify a diagnosis. If you are considering a physiotherapy assessment in Winnipeg, a few specific notes can make the appointment more useful.

sections.heading: Notice when the pain changes
paragraphs: Write down when symptoms begin, what work you were doing, and whether a break or change of position helps. Include your screen setup, driving time, sleep disruption, and any headaches or symptoms travelling into an arm. A short record over several days is more useful than trying to remember one unusually bad afternoon.

The NHS advises avoiding long periods with the neck held in one position, such as at a desk. That does not mean there is one perfect posture that prevents every episode. The practical question is whether your setup and movement habits let you vary positions comfortably. [NHS neck pain guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/neck-pain-and-stiff-neck/) explains common self-care and when to seek medical advice.

sections.heading: Know when to seek medical help
paragraphs: Neck pain with pins and needles, a cold arm, or symptoms that persist or worsen deserves medical advice. New weakness, trouble walking, or other sudden neurological symptoms need prompt assessment. Do not wait for a routine physiotherapy booking if symptoms are severe or rapidly changing. [NHS guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/neck-pain-and-stiff-neck/) gives a useful overview, though its UK service pathways do not apply in Manitoba.

sections.heading: Ask for a plan that fits your work
paragraphs: At an assessment, explain the tasks you need to do: video calls, lifting, driving, or long periods of computer work. Ask which movements you can keep doing, whether your desk setup is worth changing, how to pace activity, and what would signal that the plan needs review. A useful goal might be turning your head comfortably while driving or finishing a workday with fewer interruptions.

Pro-Motion Physiotherapy has a [neck pain service](/services/neck-pain-relief) in St. Vital. If you want a simple routine while you decide whether to book, see our existing [desk-job movement guide](/blogs/simple-stretches-to-ease-desk-job-tension). An assessment can help tailor advice to your symptoms rather than relying on a general stretch list.

sections.heading: When to book neck pain physiotherapy in St. Vital
paragraphs: If neck pain keeps returning, limits your workday, disrupts sleep, or makes driving uncomfortable, an assessment can help clarify what to do next. Bring your symptom notes and describe the tasks you want to regain. If you have new weakness, significant arm symptoms, or rapidly worsening symptoms, seek medical advice promptly rather than waiting for a routine appointment.

Pro-Motion Physiotherapy is at Unit 4 - 567 St. Anne’s Rd in St. Vital. Look for Unit 4; free parking is available in front of the clinic. Review our [neck pain service](/services/neck-pain-relief), then [check assessment availability online](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php). If you are unsure which appointment to choose or want to ask about fees, call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999). Appointment availability and treatment needs are determined individually.

title: Hip Pain While Walking in Winnipeg: When to Book Physio
excerpt: Hip pain interrupting walks or sleep? Learn what to bring to a physiotherapy assessment and how to arrange an appointment in St. Vital, Winnipeg.
intro: Hip pain is easy to describe vaguely: “it hurts when I walk.” For an assessment, it helps to be more precise. Is the pain in your groin, outside of your hip, buttock, or thigh? Does it interrupt sleep, stairs, or getting out of a car? Those details can change the questions your clinician asks.

sections.heading: Describe the activity, not only the pain score
paragraphs: Record how far you can walk before symptoms start, whether they settle with rest, and which side you sleep on. Note any recent increase in walking, lifting, or sport, plus any fall or injury. Bring a list of other health conditions and current medicines if they may affect your care.

Hip pain has more than one possible cause, so an online symptom list cannot diagnose it. The [NHS hip pain guide](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/hip-pain/) explains why pain location, sleep disruption, and the pattern of stiffness matter.

sections.heading: Some changes need medical advice sooner
paragraphs: Seek prompt medical advice if hip pain follows a fall and you cannot put weight on the leg, or if severe pain comes with a hot, swollen joint, fever, or feeling unwell. Pain that repeatedly affects sleep or normal activity also merits assessment. A routine physiotherapy appointment should not delay urgent care. See the [NHS guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/hip-pain/) for the warning signs behind this advice.

sections.heading: Questions to bring to physiotherapy
paragraphs: Ask what the examination suggests, which activities are reasonable while the cause is being clarified, and how progress will be measured. If walking is the main concern, agree on a practical baseline such as your usual route or grocery trip. If sleep is the concern, explain which position is difficult and how often it wakes you.

Pro Motion's [hip and knee service](/services/hip-knee-pain-relief) describes its assessment and exercise approach. If you also have knee pain on stairs, our [knee assessment guide](/blogs/knee-pain-stairs-winnipeg) covers that different problem. The right plan depends on the person and the findings, not on a fixed number of visits.

sections.heading: Arrange a hip pain assessment in Winnipeg
paragraphs: An assessment is worth considering when hip pain repeatedly limits a walk, interrupts sleep, or makes everyday activities harder. Bring a short record of the distance or task that causes trouble, the location of the pain, and any injury history. Severe pain after a fall or a hot swollen joint with fever needs prompt medical assessment instead of a routine physio booking.

Pro Motion's [hip and knee service](/services/hip-knee-pain-relief) is the local starting point. [Check available assessments](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php) or call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999) if you want help selecting the visit or confirming current fees. The clinic is at Unit 4, 567 St. Anne’s Road, St. Vital.

title: Wrist Pain at Work in Winnipeg: When to Book Physiotherapy
excerpt: Wrist or hand pain affecting your job? Prepare a task history, know when injury needs medical care, and book a Winnipeg physiotherapy assessment.
intro: A wrist that hurts while typing may feel very different from one that hurts while carrying a bag or using a tool. If symptoms are affecting work, record the task that brings them on. That helps a clinician look beyond the job title and understand the movement and load involved.

sections.heading: Make a short task map
paragraphs: List the activities that provoke symptoms: gripping, lifting, twisting, keyboard use, vibrating tools, or hobbies. Note which hand is affected, where pain sits, and whether you have swelling, numbness, tingling, or loss of grip. Record how long it takes to settle after the task. This is more useful than assuming every work-related wrist problem is a repetitive strain injury.
The [NHS wrist pain guide](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/hand-pain/wrist-pain/) describes several possible causes of wrist symptoms and cautions against self-diagnosis.

sections.heading: Do not treat a possible fracture as a routine strain
paragraphs: After a fall or sudden injury, severe pain, visible deformity, inability to move the wrist or hold objects, or loss of feeling calls for urgent medical advice. A hot, very swollen wrist with fever also needs prompt attention. The [NHS warning-sign guidance](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/hand-pain/wrist-pain/) explains why those changes can point to a fracture or infection.

sections.heading: Plan a workable return to tasks
paragraphs: Ask what the assessment suggests, whether a temporary task change would help, and which movements can be continued or progressed. If work is the main issue, bring examples such as tool weight, frequency, shifts, and breaks. If an injury happened at work, ask reception about claim paperwork and payment arrangements before booking; our [WCB appointment guide](/blogs/wcb-physiotherapy-winnipeg) explains what to prepare.

Pro-Motion Physiotherapy lists [elbow, wrist and hand pain care](/services/elbow-wrist-hand-pain-relief). A clinician can help decide whether your symptoms fit that service and whether another provider should be involved. This article is distinct from our [tennis elbow guide](/blogs/tennis-elbow-symptoms-physiotherapy-winnipeg), which focuses on pain at the outer elbow.

sections.heading: Book the right wrist or hand appointment
paragraphs: If gripping, typing, or tool use repeatedly limits work or daily life, a physiotherapy assessment can help you discuss the task and possible next steps. Bring a short task list and note any numbness, swelling, or loss of grip. A fall with severe pain or a changed wrist shape needs prompt medical care rather than a standard appointment.

Pro-Motion Physiotherapy offers [elbow, wrist and hand pain care](/services/elbow-wrist-hand-pain-relief) in St. Vital. [View available appointments](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php) or call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999). If the injury happened at work, tell reception before booking and ask what WCB details or authorization may be needed; a booking does not establish claim approval.

title: Knee Arthritis in Winnipeg: When to See a Physiotherapist
excerpt: Knee osteoarthritis making stairs or walks difficult? Learn what an exercise-focused physiotherapy visit can address and how to book in St. Vital.
intro: If you have knee osteoarthritis, it can be tempting to avoid movement whenever the joint feels sore. It can also be tempting to copy a demanding exercise video. Neither approach accounts for your current strength, symptoms, or goals. A physiotherapy visit can help turn “I should exercise” into a plan you can use.

sections.heading: What a useful exercise plan includes
paragraphs: Arthritis Society Canada describes aerobic activity, strength, neuromuscular exercise, and flexibility as parts of a hip or knee osteoarthritis program. The mix and starting level should be adjusted to the person. Read its [exercise guidance for hip and knee osteoarthritis](https://arthritis.ca/healthy-living/exercises-for-osteoarthritis-of-the-hip-knee/) rather than treating one online routine as a prescription.

Tell your physiotherapist what you need your knee for: stairs, getting out of a chair, walks, gardening, or work. Include what you currently do and what limits you. A plan can then connect exercises to a real activity instead of an abstract strength target.

sections.heading: Ask how to adapt when symptoms change
paragraphs: Questions worth asking include: Which movement should I start with? How often? What discomfort is acceptable for me? What should I change if the knee is more sore the next day? How will we know whether the plan is helping? These are individual decisions; a blog cannot tell you the right dose.

The [Arthritis Society's osteoarthritis overview](https://arthritis.ca/about-arthritis/arthritis-types/osteoarthritis/) describes education, self-management, and individualized exercise as components of care.

sections.heading: When to seek medical advice
paragraphs: A knee that becomes very hot and swollen, especially with fever or feeling unwell, needs prompt medical advice. So does an injury followed by inability to bear weight. If you are uncertain whether symptoms are routine for you, speak with a healthcare professional rather than increasing exercise on your own.

Pro Motion's [arthritis service](/services/arthritis-pain-relief) and [hip and knee service](/services/hip-knee-pain-relief) describe local care options. Our [knee pain on stairs guide](/blogs/knee-pain-stairs-winnipeg) is a separate starting point if stairs, rather than diagnosed osteoarthritis, are your main concern.

sections.heading: When an arthritis assessment may be useful
paragraphs: Consider an assessment if knee pain or stiffness is changing how you use stairs, walk, work, or exercise, or if a general exercise plan has been difficult to adapt. Bring your diagnosis if you have one, current activity level, and a goal that matters to you. A hot, very swollen knee with fever or an injury that prevents weight-bearing needs medical advice first.

Pro Motion describes [arthritis care](/services/arthritis-pain-relief) and [hip and knee physiotherapy](/services/hip-knee-pain-relief). [Check assessment availability](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php) at the St. Vital clinic, or call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999) to ask about appointment type and current fees. The treatment plan depends on your assessment and goals.

title: Before Joint Surgery in Winnipeg: When to Book Pre-Op Physio
excerpt: Have a hip or knee surgery date? Prepare your surgical instructions and ask whether a pre-op physiotherapy visit in Winnipeg fits your care plan.
intro: Once a surgery date is set, you may focus on the operation and leave recovery planning until afterward. Prehabilitation means preparing before treatment. For joint surgery, that can include discussing mobility, strength, daily activities, and the instructions from your surgical team. It is not a guarantee of a faster recovery.

sections.heading: Start with your own surgeon's instructions
paragraphs: Bring your planned procedure, date, written instructions, and any activity restrictions to a physiotherapy appointment. Ask what you may safely do before surgery and whether there are movements you should avoid. Generic online exercises may not suit your condition or the operation planned.

[University College London Hospitals](https://www.uclh.nhs.uk/patients-and-visitors/patient-information-pages/prehabilitation) describes prehabilitation as preparation before treatment that can involve physical, nutritional, and psychological support. Your local surgical pathway determines which parts apply to you.

sections.heading: Think about the first week at home
paragraphs: List the practical tasks that may be difficult: stairs, getting in and out of bed, bathing, food preparation, and transport to follow-up appointments. Ask your surgical team what equipment or help they recommend. A physiotherapist can discuss movement goals and questions to bring back to the team; they cannot replace the surgeon's specific precautions.

sections.heading: Questions for a pre-op assessment
paragraphs: Ask what baseline movement or strength measures would be useful, what home activity is realistic before the operation, and how the post-operative plan will be coordinated. If costs or coverage matter, confirm them with the clinic and your insurer before the visit. “Pre-op physiotherapy Winnipeg” is a service search; it does not establish that every procedure or funding program is covered.

Pro Motion describes [pre- and post-surgical care](/services/pre-post-surgical-conditions). Our [first-visit guide](/first-visit) covers what to bring and which payment questions to ask. If surgery is soon and you have new symptoms, contact your surgical team for procedure-specific advice.

sections.heading: How to arrange a pre-op physiotherapy visit
paragraphs: If your surgery date is approaching and you need help planning movement and daily tasks, ask your surgical team whether pre-operative physiotherapy is appropriate. Bring the procedure name, date, and written restrictions. Do not delay urgent or procedure-specific questions while waiting for a clinic appointment.

Pro Motion lists [pre- and post-surgical care](/services/pre-post-surgical-conditions). Call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999) before booking to confirm that the clinic can support your particular procedure and to ask about fees or program eligibility. You can also [view available assessments online](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php). The clinic is at Unit 4, 567 St. Anne’s Road in St. Vital.

title: Knee Replacement Physio in Winnipeg: Your First Visit Checklist
excerpt: After knee replacement, bring your discharge instructions and daily-life goals to a Winnipeg physiotherapy visit. Learn when and how to book in St. Vital.
intro: After knee replacement, “get back to normal” is a large and personal goal. Perhaps you want to manage stairs at home, walk to the bus, or return to a particular job. Your post-operative rehabilitation plan should start with the operation you actually had and the instructions your surgical team gave you.

sections.heading: Bring the information that sets your limits
paragraphs: Take your discharge summary, exercise sheet, follow-up dates, and any surgeon or hospital restrictions to your appointment. Tell the physiotherapist whether the operation was a total or partial replacement and about any complications or other conditions. The [NHS knee-replacement recovery guide](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/knee-replacement/recovery/) describes how hospital teams use home exercise and daily-activity advice after surgery; your own team’s instructions take priority.

sections.heading: Make progress visible in everyday activities
paragraphs: Choose two or three activities to track, such as standing from a chair, walking a familiar distance, or navigating your home’s stairs. Ask which exercises match those goals, how to progress them, and what swelling or pain change should prompt a review. Do not assume another person's timeline or online exercise list applies to your surgery.

The [Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital exercise guide](https://www.rnoh.nhs.uk/patients-and-visitors/patient-information-guides/total-knee-replacement-exercise-pack) emphasizes regular exercises and a gradual return to daily activities, while acknowledging that recovery differs between patients.

sections.heading: Know which symptoms belong with your surgical team
paragraphs: Ask before leaving hospital whom to contact about wound concerns, fever, marked new swelling, or a sudden change in function. Seek urgent medical advice for symptoms your discharge instructions identify as urgent. A routine physiotherapy booking is not a substitute for post-surgical medical assessment.

Pro Motion's [pre- and post-surgical service](/services/pre-post-surgical-conditions) covers rehabilitation planning in Winnipeg. If you are still preparing for surgery, read our [prehabilitation guide](/blogs/physiotherapy-before-joint-surgery-winnipeg) after that article is published; until then, your surgical team is the best source for procedure-specific preparation.

sections.heading: Booking post-surgical physiotherapy in St. Vital
paragraphs: Arrange rehabilitation in line with the timing and restrictions set by your surgeon or hospital. Bring your discharge notes and exercise instructions so the clinic can work from your actual care plan. For wound concerns, fever, or sudden worsening, contact your surgical team or urgent care as directed rather than waiting for physiotherapy.

Read Pro Motion's [post-surgical service information](/services/pre-post-surgical-conditions), then call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999) to confirm the right appointment and any program or insurance arrangements. You can [check available appointments online](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php). The clinic is at Unit 4, 567 St. Anne’s Road, Winnipeg.

title: Balance Concerns in Winnipeg: When to Book Fall-Prevention Physio
excerpt: A near-fall or growing balance concern is worth discussing. Learn what to bring and how to arrange a fall-prevention assessment in Winnipeg.
intro: You caught the counter before you fell. It is easy to dismiss that moment because there was no injury. Yet a near-fall can be a useful prompt to look at balance, strength, footwear, vision, medication effects, and the environment. The goal is to understand what happened, not to assume that age alone explains it.

sections.heading: Keep a simple near-fall record
paragraphs: Write down where you were, what you were doing, whether you felt dizzy or tripped, and how you recovered. Include lighting, footwear, any walking aid, and whether a similar incident has happened before. That description helps distinguish a slippery step from a pattern of unsteadiness.

The [Public Health Agency of Canada](https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/health-promotion/aging-seniors/preventing-falls-injuries-older-adults.html) lists balance, muscle strength, vision, footwear, and tripping hazards among factors that can affect fall risk.

sections.heading: Check more than exercise
paragraphs: If you have dizziness, fainting, new weakness, or a sudden change in walking, seek medical advice rather than assuming you just need balance exercises. Ask a doctor or pharmacist whether medicines might contribute to dizziness; arrange a vision check if needed. At home, remove obvious trip hazards and consider the surfaces you walk on, including Winnipeg's icy seasons.

Canada's [fall-prevention guidance](https://www.canada.ca/en/public-health/services/health-promotion/aging-seniors/preventing-falls-injuries-older-adults.html) recommends both safer environments and strength and balance activity.

sections.heading: What to ask at a physiotherapy visit
paragraphs: Ask what the assessment found, which activities are safe to practise, whether a walking aid should be reviewed, and how to measure changes in confidence and function. Tell the clinician about any fall or near-fall, even when you were not hurt. A personalized plan may differ from a generic home exercise handout.

Pro Motion lists a [fall-prevention service](/services/fall-prevention). Its existing [fall-prevention article](/blogs/fall-prevention-physiotherapy-in-winnipeg-protecting-seniors-from-the-rising-risk-of-falls) focuses on exercises; this guide focuses on what to do after a near-fall.

sections.heading: When to arrange a balance assessment
paragraphs: If you have nearly fallen more than once, have started avoiding normal activities because of balance concerns, or feel less steady during everyday walking, discuss an assessment. Bring a record of what happened and any walking aid you use. Sudden new weakness, fainting, or severe dizziness needs medical advice promptly instead of a routine fall-prevention visit.

Pro Motion's [fall-prevention service](/services/fall-prevention) describes the local assessment. To ask whether it suits your situation, call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999), or [view available appointments](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php). The clinic is at Unit 4, 567 St. Anne’s Road in St. Vital, Winnipeg.

title: Shoulder Pain in Winnipeg: Rotator Cuff or Frozen Shoulder?
excerpt: Pain, weakness or stiffness can have different causes. Learn what to describe and when to book a shoulder assessment in St. Vital, Winnipeg.
intro: Shoulder pain can make two everyday tasks equally difficult: reaching up to a cupboard and putting on a coat. Those tasks do not tell you on their own whether the problem involves a rotator cuff tendon, a stiff shoulder joint, or something else. An assessment looks at your history, movement and strength rather than selecting a diagnosis from one symptom.

sections.heading: Describe how it began and what is limited
paragraphs: Tell the clinician whether symptoms followed a fall or lift, developed gradually, or came with increasing stiffness. Note which movements hurt, which movements feel physically blocked, and whether night pain affects sleep. Mention any marked weakness or previous shoulder surgery. You do not need to arrive with a self-diagnosis.
The [NHS shoulder pain guide](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/shoulder-pain/) lists several possible causes and advises against diagnosing yourself from a symptom chart.

sections.heading: Why the distinction matters
paragraphs: Frozen shoulder often involves substantial stiffness; rotator cuff-related problems can involve pain or weakness with arm use. These patterns can overlap, and only a clinician can interpret them in context. [AAOS information on rotator cuff tears](https://orthoinfo.aaos.org/globalassets/pdfs/rotator-cuff-tears.pdf) describes how treatment choices depend on the tear and a person's needs. Our separate [frozen shoulder guide](/blogs/frozen-shoulder-physiotherapy-winnipeg) explains that condition in more detail.

sections.heading: Seek medical care for sudden or severe changes
paragraphs: Sudden severe shoulder pain after an injury, a changed shoulder shape, inability to move the arm, persistent numbness, or feeling unwell with a hot swollen shoulder calls for urgent medical advice. The [NHS warning signs](https://www.nhs.uk/symptoms/shoulder-pain/) explain when routine self-care is not enough.

For a non-urgent concern, ask at Pro Motion's [shoulder pain service](/services/shoulder-pain-relief) what the assessment will cover and how you will judge progress. The existing [overhead-reaching article](/blogs/shoulder-pain-reaching-overhead-winnipeg) helps you prepare a task history.

sections.heading: When to book a shoulder assessment
paragraphs: If shoulder symptoms keep you from reaching, lifting, dressing, or sleeping comfortably, an assessment can help clarify the next step. Bring details of any injury and what movements feel painful or restricted. Sudden severe pain after a fall, a changed shoulder shape, or loss of feeling in the arm needs prompt medical care.

Pro Motion's [shoulder pain service](/services/shoulder-pain-relief) is in St. Vital. [Check assessment availability](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php), or call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999) if you are unsure which visit to select. An online article cannot confirm whether your symptoms are a rotator cuff problem, frozen shoulder, or another condition.

title: Knee Pain While Running in Winnipeg: When to See a Physio
excerpt: Knee pain during or after runs? Bring your training history to a sports physiotherapy assessment in Winnipeg and ask about a safe return plan.
intro: A knee can feel fine for the first kilometre and ache after the third. Or the run may feel manageable but stairs are painful the next morning. Those patterns matter when you are deciding how to return to training. There is no single “runner's knee” diagnosis that explains every painful run.

sections.heading: Bring your training pattern
paragraphs: Write down your usual weekly distance, recent changes in distance or pace, hills, surfaces, shoes, and any strength work. Note where pain sits, when it begins, whether it changes your stride, and what happens later that day and the next morning. If swelling appears, record when it started. This gives a physiotherapist a useful starting point for assessment.

The [NHS running-injury guide](https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/knee-pain-and-other-running-injuries/) notes that knee pain can have several causes and advises medical or physiotherapy review when it persists.

sections.heading: Ask about readiness, not a fixed date
paragraphs: Questions to ask include: What activity can I do while the knee settles? What would show that I am ready to try a short run? How should I increase running without guessing? What pain or swelling change means I should stop and be reassessed? The answer depends on the cause, the severity, and your response to activity; a blog cannot set your timetable.

[Berkshire Healthcare NHS](https://www.berkshirehealthcare.nhs.uk/advice/return-to-running-programme) describes gradual return-to-running principles and flags worsening pain and persistent joint swelling as reasons to reassess.

sections.heading: Know when to seek prompt care
paragraphs: Seek medical advice promptly for a severe injury, a very swollen knee, inability to bear weight, or symptoms that are rapidly worsening. If the issue is less urgent but keeps recurring, a physiotherapy assessment can help connect running demands with strength, movement, and recovery habits.

Pro Motion's [sports injury service](/services/sports-injuries) is the relevant local starting point. If your main difficulty is stairs rather than running, our [knee pain on stairs guide](/blogs/knee-pain-stairs-winnipeg) addresses that question separately.

sections.heading: When to book a running assessment
paragraphs: If knee pain keeps returning when you run, changes your stride, or lingers into the next day, a sports-injury assessment can help you decide what to change and when to progress. Bring your training log and note any swelling or previous injury. Severe swelling or inability to bear weight needs medical attention sooner.

Pro Motion's [sports injury service](/services/sports-injuries) is a local starting point. [View available assessments](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php) or call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999) to ask which appointment fits your concern. The clinic is at Unit 4, 567 St. Anne’s Road in St. Vital, Winnipeg.

title: Returning to Work After Injury in Winnipeg: Is Reconditioning Right?
excerpt: A physically demanding job needs a task-specific return plan. Learn what to bring and how to ask about work reconditioning in Winnipeg.
intro: “I can lift a box once” is different from “I can lift, carry, and repeat that task throughout a shift.” After an injury, the goal of work reconditioning is to connect rehabilitation with the actual demands of your job. A useful assessment begins with what the work requires and what you can currently do.

sections.heading: Describe your job in concrete terms
paragraphs: Bring a job description if you have one, but add the details it may omit: weights, repetitions, awkward positions, walking distance, shift length, breaks, and equipment. Explain which parts you can do now and what changes during or after a shift. If modified duties are available, describe them too. A clear task history makes it easier to discuss realistic goals.

Pro Motion's [work-injury service](/services/work-injuries) includes return-to-work planning. The clinic also describes a work-reconditioning approach in its treatment information; ask reception whether that service fits your situation.

sections.heading: Separate rehabilitation from claim administration
paragraphs: If the injury happened at work, follow your employer's and WCB Manitoba's reporting instructions. A physiotherapy appointment does not itself open or approve a claim. Keep your injury date, claim details, and any written restrictions together. Our [WCB physiotherapy checklist](/blogs/wcb-physiotherapy-winnipeg) covers the administrative questions to ask before booking.
[WCB Manitoba's worker guidance](https://www.wcb.mb.ca/workers) is the official source for claim processes; check it for current steps rather than relying on a clinic blog.

sections.heading: Agree on measures that match the job
paragraphs: Ask how your capacity will be assessed and progressed, which tasks can be practised safely, and what symptoms or fatigue should trigger a change. If another clinician has set restrictions, bring those instructions so your rehabilitation plan is aligned. A gradual return may involve discussion among you, the treating professionals, the employer, and the insurer, depending on the claim.

The next step is a task-specific assessment, not a promised number of sessions or return date. Use the [first-visit guide](/first-visit) for clinic preparation and ask reception about current appointment and payment arrangements.

sections.heading: Ask about a work-focused assessment
paragraphs: If lifting, carrying, standing, or long shifts remain difficult after injury, ask whether work-focused rehabilitation fits your situation. Bring your job demands, current restrictions, and any insurer or employer paperwork. A clinician can discuss goals and next steps after assessment; no blog can promise a return-to-work date.

Pro Motion's [work-injury service](/services/work-injuries) describes the local care offered. Call [(204) 560-2999](tel:+12045602999) before booking to confirm that work reconditioning is appropriate and to ask about any WCB or insurer authorization. You can also [view available assessments online](https://pmphysio.juvonno.com/portal/publicbook.php). An appointment alone does not approve a claim.
